newsitem.title: IRAQ: Arabs in Iraq protest against U.S. attacks.
newsitem.headline: Arabs in Iraq protest against U.S. attacks.

text.p: Thousands of Arabs demonstrated against U.S. missile attacks on Iraq and burned an effigy of U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday.

"Your aggression on Iraq is an aggression against the whole Arab nation," the demonstrators, who carried portraits of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, chanted as they marched to the U.N. coordinator's office in Baghdad.

The demonstrators were Arabs residents of Iraq, most of whom came from Yemen, Sudan, Jordan and Tunisia -- countries who sympathised with Baghdad during the U.S.-led Gulf War that ejected Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991.
Western reporters covered the demonstration under official escort.
The demonstrators burned an effigy of Clinton and the flags of the United States and Britain.

The United States fired 44 cruise missiles at air defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday. Britain strongly supported the U.S. attacks which were prompted by the Iraqi army's incursion into Kurdish areas in northern Iraq on Saturday.
"Down, down U.S.A ...Down, down Bill Clinton," the demonstrators chanted. "We are with you Saddam, until you achieve full liberation," a banner carried by the protesters read.
They submitted a written message addressed to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali urging him to take approperiate measures to stop the American missile attacks.
